Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 41, verse 16:

There is no doubt that the days on which Allah, glorified is He, inflicted punishment upon His enemies and the enemies of His messengers were days of misfortune (nuḥūs) for them, because misfortune befell them therein. Although they were days of good for His believing friends (awliyā'), they were a misfortune for the deniers and a good fortune for the believers.

This is also the case with the Day of Resurrection, for it is grievous for the disbelievers, a day of misfortune for them, and easy for the believers, a day of good fortune for them.

Mujāhid said: "Ayyāman naḥsāt" means "ill-omened days" (mashā'īm).

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: its meaning is "severe," that is, severe in cold, so that the cold was a scourge (hadhdhāb) for them.

Abū ʿAlī said: al-Aṣmaʿī recited, using naḥs in the sense of cold:

"As if the wine's essence was presented with naḥs, which makes the clear water turn to ice (ynḥīl shafīfuhā al-mā' al-zalāl)."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "naḥsāt" means "consecutive, successive." Likewise is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind in a day of ill omen, continuous﴾.

The day was a misfortune for them because the punishment was sent upon them therein, meaning it did not cease for them, unlike the calamities of this world which come and go. Rather, this misfortune is perpetual upon these deniers of the messengers.

"Mustamirr" is an attribute of the misfortune (naḥs), not of the day. Whoever thinks it is an attribute of the day, and that it was a Wednesday, the last Wednesday of the month, and that this day is perpetually unlucky, has erred and misunderstood the Qur'an. The day in question is according to what occurs in it: how many blessings Allah bestows on His friends on this day, and how many trials and punishments He brings upon His enemies therein, just as this occurs on other days. Thus the good fortune and misfortune of days is only due to the good fortune and misfortune of deeds, their conformity to the pleasure of the Lord, and the misfortune of deeds is only through their opposition to what the messengers brought.

One day may be a day of good fortune for one group and a misfortune for another, just as the Day of Badr was a day of good fortune for the believers and a day of misfortune for the disbelievers.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 41, verse 17:

It means: We made it clear to them and made them aware, so they recognized the truth and were certain of it, yet they preferred blindness to it. Thus the disbelief of these people was born of ignorance.

(Benefit)

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾

This is guidance after clarification and indication, and it is a condition, not a necessary cause. If it is not accompanied by another guidance after it, the perfection of guidance is not attained through it, and this is the guidance of divine success (tawfiq) and inspiration (ilham).

This clarification is of two kinds: clarification by the recited, audible verses, and clarification by the observed, visible signs. Both are proofs and signs of the Oneness of God, His names, His attributes, His perfection, and the truthfulness of what His messengers reported about Him. For this reason He calls His servants, through His recited verses, to reflect upon His observed signs, and He urges them to think upon both. This clarification is what the messengers were sent with, and it was entrusted to them and, after them, to the scholars. After that, God misguides whom He wills. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make clear to them. Then God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Ibrahim: 4]. So the messengers make clear, and it is God who misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, by His might and His wisdom.

(Section)

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

His statement: "The obligation of a thing by the law does not entail its existence in the senses. Therefore he mentioned what exists through it after mentioning what is obligated through it, namely the illumination of the Truth, the Exalted." His intent is the complete illumination from which guidance does not differ. Otherwise, a servant may see the truth and guidance may not come from him, as the Exalted said: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17].

He, glory be to Him, gave them insight, but they preferred error over guidance. The Exalted also said: ﴿Satan made their deeds attractive to them and barred them from the way, though they were discerning﴾ [al-Ankabut: 38]. And the Exalted said: ﴿God would never misguide a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against﴾ [al-Tawbah: 115].

The Exalted said concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿They denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

This insight did not necessitate the existence of guidance, because He, glory be to Him, did not will its existence; He willed only the existence of mere insight. What He willed occurred, and what He did not will did not occur.

As for complete illumination, it necessitates the existence of guidance. It is what He commanded us to ask Him for in every prayer, and the people of Paradise said of it: ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

The Exalted said: ﴿God invites to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [Yunus: 25].

So by His call He generalized the clarification and indication, and by His guidance He specified divine success and inspiration. Had the Shaykh said, "It is found through God's success after His illumination," it would have been better, and perhaps this is what he intended, and God knows best.

These people assumed that Allah does not know some particulars, so how much more so those who assume that He has no knowledge, no hearing, no sight, no speech, does not speak, did not establish Himself on His Throne, has no true action by which He governs the affair, and has no wisdom for which He does what He does?!

Those people also permitted that He might not help His Messenger, and that He might turn the calamity back upon him and upon the believers.

(Section)

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after a lengthy discussion:

And like some people's reliance on his ﷺ saying, relating from his Lord:

"I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he wishes."

That is, whatever he thinks of Me, I will do to him. There is no doubt that good opinion of Allah occurs only together with good conduct, for the one who does good has a good opinion of his Lord: that He will reward him for his good deeds, not break His promise, and accept his repentance.

As for the evildoer who persists in major sins, injustice and transgressions, the sense of alienation caused by sins, injustice and the unlawful prevents him from having a good opinion of his Lord. This is observable among people: the runaway slave who has departed from his master's obedience does not have a good opinion of him, and good opinion never coexists with the alienation of wrongdoing. The wrongdoer is estranged in proportion to his wrongdoing, and the people with the best opinion of their Lord are the most obedient to Him.

As al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer thinks well of his Lord, so he acts well; and the wicked person thinks badly of his Lord, so he acts badly."

How can one who turns away from Him, who is constantly journeying in the things that displease Him and anger Him, be one who has a good opinion of his Lord? He exposes himself to His curse, His right and His command have become insignificant to him so he neglects them, His prohibition has become insignificant to him so he commits what is forbidden and persists in it? How can one have a good opinion of his Lord when he wages war against Him, opposes His friends, allies himself with His enemies, denies the attributes of His perfection, has a bad opinion of what He has described Himself with and what His Messenger ﷺ has described Him with, and in his ignorance supposes that the apparent meaning of that is misguidance and disbelief?

And how can one have a good opinion of his Lord when he assumes that He does not speak, does not command, does not forbid, is not pleased and does not become angry?

Allah has said concerning one who doubts that His hearing encompasses some particulars, and that is the hidden speech: ﴿And that is your opinion which you thought of your Lord; it has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers﴾ [Fussilat: 23].

So these people, when they assumed that Allah, glorified is He, does not know much of what they do, this was an evil opinion of their Lord, and that opinion brought them to ruin. This is the condition of everyone who denies the attributes of His perfection and the descriptions of His majesty, and describes Him with what does not befit Him. If such a person thinks that He will admit him to Paradise, this is delusion and self-deception from his own soul, and an enticement from Satan, not a good opinion of his Lord.

So reflect on this point, and reflect on how greatly one needs it, and how there can coexist in the servant's heart his certainty that he will meet Allah, that Allah hears and sees his place, knows his secret and his public, that nothing of his affair is hidden from Him, that he will be made to stand before Him and will be questioned about everything he did, while he persists in what displeases Him, neglects His commands and leaves His rights unfulfilled, yet still has a good opinion of Him. Is this anything other than the deceptions of the souls and the delusions of wishful thinking?

Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf said: "Myself and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr entered upon 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she said: 'If you had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during an illness he had, and I had six or seven dinars, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to distribute them. She said: The pain of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ occupied me until Allah granted him health. Then he asked me about them, saying: What did you do? Did you distribute the six dinars?

I said: No, by Allah, your pain occupied me. She said: He called for them, placed them in his palm, and said: What would the opinion of the Prophet of Allah be if he met Allah while these were in his possession? And in another wording: What would the opinion of Muhammad be of his Lord if he met Allah while these were with him?'"

Alas, what then is the opinion of the people of major sins and the wrongdoers of Allah when they meet Him while the injustices against people are with them? If it would benefit them to say, "We have had a good opinion of You, that You will not punish a wrongdoer or a sinner," then let the servant do whatever he wishes, let him commit everything Allah has forbidden him, and let him have a good opinion of Allah, for the Fire will not touch him. Glory be to Allah! How far does delusion reach the servant! Ibrahim had already said to his people: ﴿Is it falsehood, gods other than Allah that you desire? So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [As-Saffat: 86–87].

That is: What is your opinion of what He will do with you when you meet Him, having worshipped other than Him?

Whoever reflects truly upon this point will know that good opinion of Allah is itself good action, for the servant is moved to good action by his opinion of his Lord, that He will reward him for his deeds, grant him reward for them, and accept them from him. So what moved him to action was good opinion, and whenever his opinion of Allah is good, his action is good. Otherwise, good opinion accompanied by following one's desires is incapacity, as in the hadith of al-Tirmidhi and al-Musnad (Imam Ahmad's collection of hadith) from Shaddad ibn Aws, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The intelligent one is the one who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is the one who follows his desires and wishes upon Allah."

In sum, good opinion of Allah occurs only where the causes of salvation are established, but where the causes of destruction are established, good opinion cannot be realized.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on surah 41, verse 24:

That is: if they seek to have us relent (iʿtāb) and to remove our displeasure (ʿatb) toward them. It is said: "ʿatiba ʿalayhi" when he turned away from him and was angry with him.

Then it is said: "istaʿtaba al-sayyidu ʿabdahu," meaning the master asked his servant to remove his own displeasure from him by returning to his good pleasure.

And "aʿtabtu ʿabdī" means I removed his displeasure through his obedience. It is also said: "istaʿtaba al-ʿabdu sayyidahu," meaning the servant asked his master to remove his anger and displeasure from him, so his master "aʿtabahu," that is, removed his displeasure from him.

On this basis, the words of the Exalted, ﴿And if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased﴾, mean: if they seek our relenting, which is the removal of our displeasure from them, then they will not be among those whose displeasure is removed. For in the Hereafter their slips are not overlooked, and their repentance is not accepted.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 41, verse 25:

Al-Kalbi said: "We assigned to them companions from among the devils."

Muqatil said: "We prepared for them companions from among the devils."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "What is before them of the affairs of this world and what is behind them of the affairs of the Hereafter."

The meaning is: they made the world appealing to them until they preferred it, and they called them to deny the Hereafter and turn away from it.

Al-Kalbi also said: "They made appealing to them what is before them of the affairs of the Hereafter, namely that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection; and what is behind them of the affairs of this world, namely the misguidance they were upon."

This is the view chosen by al-Farra'.

Ibn Zayd said: "They made appealing to them the past evil of their deeds and what they would go on to do of it."

The meaning according to this view is: they made appealing to them what they had done and did not repent from, and what they were resolved upon and did not intend to abandon.

This descent occurs at death, in the grave, and at resurrection, and the first of the good tidings of the Hereafter comes at death.

(Section)

One of the early Muslims (salaf) said: When the son of Adam rises in the morning, an angel and a devil approach him. If he remembers Allah, glorifies Him, praises Him, and declares His oneness (tahlil), the devil is driven away and the angel takes charge of him. If he begins the day with anything else, the angel leaves him and the devil takes charge of him.

The angel continues to draw near the servant until authority, obedience, and dominance belong to him. The angels then take charge of him during his life, at his death, and at his resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."﴾ [Fussilat: 30-31].

When the angel takes charge of a person, he takes charge of the most sincere, most beneficial, and most righteous of creatures. He makes him firm, teaches him, strengthens his heart, and Allah supports him, as Allah said: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels, "I am with you, so make firm those who have believed"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

So at death the angel says: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of that which will delight you." He makes him firm with the firm word, at the time when he most needs it in this world, at death, and in the grave when he is questioned.

No one is more beneficial to the servant than the companionship of the angel. He is his guardian in his wakefulness and his sleep, in his life, at his death, and in his grave. He is his companion in his loneliness, his friend in his solitude, his interlocutor in his secret thoughts. He fights his enemy on his behalf, defends him, helps him against them, promises him good, gives him good news of it, and urges him to affirm the truth. This is as in the report related both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and as a mawquf (traced to a Companion): "The angel has an inspiration (lamma) in the heart of the son of Adam, and the devil has an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel is a promise of good and affirmation of the promise, and the inspiration of the devil is a promise of evil and denial of the truth."

When the angel draws very near to the servant, he speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the upright word. When the angel withdraws and the devil draws near, the devil speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the word of falsehood and obscenity, until a man is seen speaking with the tongue of an angel, and another speaking with the tongue of a devil.

It is related in a hadith: "Indeed, tranquility (sakinah) speaks upon the tongue of 'Umar" (may Allah be pleased with him). Some of them would hear a good word from a righteous man and say: "Only an angel has cast that upon your tongue." And if they heard its opposite, they would say: "Only a devil has cast that upon your tongue." The angel casts truth into the heart and upon the tongue, while the devil casts falsehood into the heart and sends it onto the tongue.

Among the consequences of sins is that they drive away from the servant his guardian, whose happiness lies in his nearness, neighborhood, and friendship, and they bring near to him his enemy, whose wretchedness, destruction, and corruption lie in his nearness and friendship. To the point that the angel defends the servant and repels on his behalf when a fool insults him and reviles him. Just as two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ), one of them reviling the other while he remained silent. Then he spoke one word in reply to his companion. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I replied to him with some of his own words, you stood up." He said: "The angel was defending you, but when you replied to him, the devil came, and I would not sit with him."

When a Muslim servant prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says "Amin" to his prayer and says: "And for you the same."

When he finishes reciting al-Fatihah, the angels say "Amin" to his supplication.

When a servant who is a monotheist and follows the path and sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) sins, the bearers of the Throne and those around it ask forgiveness for him.

When the servant sleeps in a state of wudu', he spends the night in the protection of an angel.

So the angel of the believer repels evil from him, fights and defends him, teaches him, makes him firm, and encourages him. It is not fitting for a person to mistreat his guardian, to go to great lengths to harm him, to drive him away, or to banish him, for he is his guest and his neighbor.

If honoring the guest is among human obligations, and kindness to the neighbor is among the requirements and demands of faith, then what is the expectation of honoring the most noble of guests and the best and most righteous of neighbors? When a servant harms the angel through various kinds of disobedience, injustice, and immorality, the angel calls down upon him from his Lord and says: "May Allah not reward you with good," just as he prays for him when he honors him with obedience and goodness.

One of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Indeed, there is with you one who never leaves you, so be modest before them and honor them."

No one is more base than the one who is not modest before the Noble, the Mighty in station, nor reveres Him nor honors Him. Allah the Glorified has drawn attention to this meaning with His saying: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12]. That is, be modest before these noble guardians, honor them, and respect them by not letting them see from you what you would be ashamed for another like yourself to see you doing. The angels are hurt by what the children of Adam are hurt by. If the son of Adam is hurt by one who commits immorality and disobedience before him, even if that person does the same deed, then what is the expectation regarding the harm to the noble recording angels? And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

The motivation of religion, compared with the motivation of desire, has three states:

The first: that the dominance and power belong to the call of religion, so the army of desire is turned back in chains. This is attained only through constant patience. Those who reach this rank are the ones granted victory in this world and the Hereafter, and they are those who said: ﴿Our Lord is Allah, then they remained steadfast﴾.

They are those to whom the angels will say at death: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

They are those who attained the companionship of Allah, who is with the patient, and they are those who strove for Allah with the striving due to Him, and whom He singled out for His guidance over all others.

The second state: that the power and dominance belong to the call of desire, so the motivation of religion is completely eliminated, and the wretched one submits to Satan and his troops, who lead him wherever they wish. He has two conditions with them. One is that he becomes one of their soldiers and helpers; this is the state of the weak and powerless. The second is that Satan becomes one of his soldiers; this is the state of the corrupt, dominant sinner and the innovator who is a caller and is followed, as the poet said:

"I was a man of the army of Iblis, then my state rose until Iblis became one of my soldiers."

So Iblis and his troops become his helpers and followers. These are the ones whose wretchedness overcame them, who sold the life of this world for the Hereafter. They reached this state only because they were bankrupt of patience. This state is the state of severe trial, the depth of misery, bad destiny, and the gloating of enemies. Its soldiers are deceit, trickery, false wishes, delusion, procrastination in deeds, long hope, and preferring the immediate over the lasting. About the one who is in this state the Prophet said: "The incapable one is the one who follows his desires and wishes from Allah." The people of this state are of many kinds:

Among them is the one who wars against Allah and His Messenger, striving to extinguish what the Messenger brought, who blocks the way of Allah and seeks to make it crooked and distorted with all his effort, so as to turn people away from it.

Among them is the one who turns away from what the Messenger brought, who is occupied only with his worldly life and its desires.

Among them is the hypocrite with two faces, who earns his living through both disbelief and Islam.

Among them is the frivolous mocker who wastes his breath on lewdness, amusement, and play.

Among them is one who, when admonished, says: "Oh, how I long to repent, but it has become impossible for me, and I have no hope in it."

Among them is one who says: "Allah does not need my prayer or fasting, and I will not be saved by my deeds, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Among them is one who says: "Abandoning sins is a belittling of Allah's pardon and forgiveness."

"So commit as many sins as you can, if you are going to meet the Generous One."

Among them is one who says: "What is my obedience worth compared to what I have done? What benefit is a finger's rescue to a drowning man whose body remains drowned?"

Among them is one who says: "I will repent later, and when death comes and descends upon my courtyard, I will repent, and my repentance will be accepted..."

And other kinds of the deluded whose minds have fallen into the hands of their desires. None of them uses his mind except in the subtle tricks by which he reaches the fulfillment of his lust.

His mind, in the hands of Satan, is like a captive in the hand of an unbeliever, who uses it to tend pigs, press wine, and carry the cross. By subduing his mind and surrendering it to his enemies, he is, in the sight of Allah, like a man who overpowers a Muslim, sells him to the unbelievers, hands him over to them, and makes him their captive.

(Section)

Here is a wondrous point that must be grasped, and the heart should be cleared to reflect upon it. It is that this deluded person, when he humiliated the authority of Allah, by which Allah honored him, raised his rank, and placed him in the hand of the most hateful of His enemies, making him a captive under their domination, control, and authority, Allah then set over him the one whose right it was to have power over him. He placed him under the domination, control, and authority of that enemy, who subjugates him as he wishes, mocks him, and mocks his soldiers and party. Just as he humiliated the authority of Allah and handed it to His enemy, Allah humiliated him and set over him his enemy, whom He had commanded to have power over him, to humiliate and subdue him. He became like one who surrendered himself to his most hostile enemy, who inflicts on him the worst torment. He was about to be taken captive, subdued, and have his rage quenched by his enemy. When he abandoned resistance and fighting and submitted to him, Allah imposed on him that enemy as a punishment. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who make him their ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾

(Section: The Station of Steadfastness)

Section: The Station of Steadfastness

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is the station of steadfastness (istiqamah).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13].

And He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and those who have turned back with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [Hud: 112].

So He clarified that steadfastness is the opposite of transgression, which is exceeding the limits in everything.

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "I am only a human like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God, so take a straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness."﴾ [Fussilat: 6].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had remained upon the way, We would have given them abundant water to test them therein.﴾ [al-Jinn: 16].

The most truthful of this community and the greatest in steadfastness, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), was asked about steadfastness. He said: "That you do not associate anything with Allah." He meant steadfastness upon pure monotheism.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Steadfastness is that you remain steadfast upon the command and the prohibition, and do not swerve like a fox."

'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Istaqamu: they made their deeds sincerely for Allah."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Istaqamu: they performed the obligatory duties."

Al-Hasan said: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, so they acted in obedience to Him and avoided His disobedience."

Mujahid said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Allah."

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah sanctify his spirit) say: "They remained steadfast upon His love and worship, so they did not turn away from Him to the right or to the left."

In Sahih Muslim, from Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying in Islam about which I will not ask anyone other than you.' He said: 'Say: I believe in Allah, then remain steadfast.'"

Also in it, from Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count it all. And know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains wudu' except a believer."

What is required of the servant is steadfastness, which is rectitude. If he cannot achieve it, then closeness to it (muqarabah). If he falls short of that, then negligence and waste. As in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Be upright and seek closeness to uprightness. And know that none of you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

In this hadith he gathered all the stations of religion. He commanded steadfastness, which is rectitude and correctness in intentions, words, and deeds.

In the hadith of Thawban, he informed that they cannot sustain it, so he moved them to muqarabah, which is that they come close to steadfastness according to their capacity, like one who shoots at a target: if he does not hit it, he comes close to it. Yet with this, he informed them that neither steadfastness nor closeness saves on the Day of Resurrection, so no one should rely on his deed, nor be pleased with it, nor think that his salvation lies in it. Rather, his salvation is only through the mercy, pardon, and grace of Allah.

So steadfastness is a comprehensive word, grasping the totality of religion. It is standing before Allah with the reality of truthfulness and fulfillment of the covenant.

Steadfastness relates to words, actions, states, and intentions. In steadfastness regarding them is that they are for Allah, through Allah, and upon the command of Allah.

Some of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: "Be a possessor of steadfastness (istiqamah), not a seeker of miracles (karamah). For your soul is restless in seeking miracles, while your Lord demands of you steadfastness."

And I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God sanctify his spirit, say: "The greatest of miracles is adherence to steadfastness."

[Section: The Degrees of Steadfastness]

[The First Degree: Steadfastness in striving with moderation (iqtisad)]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree: steadfastness in striving with moderation (iqtisad). Neither being content with the mere outward form of knowledge (rasm al-ʿilm), nor exceeding the bounds of sincerity (ikhlas), nor opposing the way of the Sunnah (nahj al-Sunnah).

This degree comprises six matters: action (ʿamal) and striving (ijtihad) in it, which is the exertion of effort; and moderation (iqtisad), which is walking between the two extremes of excess (ifrat), namely oppressing the souls, and deficiency (tafrit) through neglect; and halting at what knowledge has drawn (yarsumuhu al-ʿilm), not halting at the call of the moment (daʿi al-hal); and singling out the One Worshipped with intention, which is sincerity; and the actions conforming to the command, which is following the Sunnah.

By these six matters the steadfastness of the people of this degree is completed. By departing from any one of them they depart from steadfastness: either a total departure or a partial departure.

The predecessors (salaf) often mention these two principles, namely moderation in actions and holding fast to the Sunnah, for Satan smells the heart of the servant and tests it. If he sees in it a call to innovation (bidʿah) and an aversion from full submission to the Sunnah, he removes it from holding fast to it. If he sees in it eagerness for the Sunnah and intense pursuit of it, he does not succeed through cutting it off from the Sunnah, so he orders it to strive, to oppress the soul, and to exceed the limit of moderation in it, saying: "This is good and obedience, and increase and striving in it is more perfect." So do not slacken with those who slacken, nor sleep with those who sleep. He does not cease urging and inciting him until he takes him out of moderation in it, so he exits its limit, just as the first one exits this limit. Likewise this other one exits the other limit.

This is the condition of the Khawarij, whom the people of steadfastness regard as belittling their prayer alongside their prayer, their fasting alongside their fasting, and their recitation alongside their recitation. Both matters are a departure from the Sunnah into innovation. But this one leads to the innovation of deficiency and neglect, and the other to the innovation of excess and extravagance.

And one of the predecessors said: "God has not commanded any command except that Satan has in it two tendencies: either toward deficiency (tafrit), or toward exceeding the bounds, which is excess (ifrat); and he does not care which of the two he attains: increase or decrease."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may God be pleased with them both: "O ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, every doer has a surge of zeal (shirrah), and every surge has a lull (fatrah). Whoever's lull is toward the Sunnah has succeeded, and whoever's lull is toward innovation has perished and lost." He said this to him when he ordered him to moderation in action.

So all good lies in striving with moderation, and sincerity joined with following. As one of the Companions said: "Moderation on the path and the Sunnah is better than striving in opposition to the path and the Sunnah. So be eager that your actions be upon the methodology of the Prophets, peace be upon them, and their Sunnah."

Likewise, showing off (riyaʾ) in actions removes one from steadfastness, and so does lassitude and laxity (futur wa tawani).

[Section: The Second Degree: Steadfastness of States (istiqamat al-ahwal)]

He said: The second degree is steadfastness of states (ahwal). It is witnessing the Reality (shuhud al-haqiqah) not as acquisition (kasb); abandoning claim (rafd al-daʿwa) not as knowledge (ʿilm); and remaining with the light of wakefulness (yaqazah) not as self-guarding (tahaffuz).

He means that the steadfastness of the state is by these three.

As for witnessing the Reality: the Reality is of two realities: a cosmic reality (haqiqah kawniyyah) and a religious reality (haqiqah diniyyah), and a third reality gathers them, which is their source, their origin, and their end. Most of the practitioners of the path (arbab al-suluk) among the later ones only mean by the Reality the cosmic reality. Witnessing it is witnessing the singularity of the Lord in action, and that all else is a locus for the flow of His rulings and His acts. It is like a ditch which is merely a place for water to flow through.

They believe that witnessing this reality and annihilation (fana') in it is the ultimate goal of the wayfarers.

Among them are those who witness the reality of eternity (azaliyyah) and perpetuity, and the annihilation and folding of contingent things within the expanse of eternity and everlastingness, and their dissolving therein. So they witness them as non-existent, and witness the singularity of their Originator with true existence through the Truth, and that the existence of all else is traces and shadows.

The first witnessed His singularity in acts; this one witnessed His singularity in existence.

The possessor of the religious reality is in another stage, for he is in the station of command and prohibition, reward and punishment, loyalty and enmity, and the distinction between what God loves and is pleased with, and what He hates and is angered by. He is in the station of the second distinction (al-farq al-thani), which the servant does not attain the level of Islam—let alone the station of ihsan—except by it.

Whoever turns away from it entirely has no share in Islam whatsoever. He is like the one whom al-Junayd used to advise his companions about, saying: "Hold fast to the second distinction." It was called "second" because the first distinction is a distinction by nature and the self, while this is a distinction by the command.

Unification (jamʿ) is also of two kinds: unification within distinction (jamʿ fi farq), which is the unification of the people of steadfastness and monotheism; and unification without distinction (jamʿ bila farq), which is the unification of the people of heresy (zandaqah) and atheism (ilhad).

So people are of three types: the possessor of distinction without unification, who is blameworthy, deficient, and forsaken.

The possessor of unification without distinction, which is the unification of the people of heresy and atheism: his companion is an atheist heretic (zindiq).

The possessor of distinction and unification: he witnesses the distinction within the unification and the multiplicity within the oneness. He is the upright monotheist who distinguishes. This is the possessor of the third reality, which gathers the religious and the cosmic realities. Witnessing this gathering reality is the very essence of steadfastness.

As for witnessing the cosmic reality, or the eternal one, and annihilation in it: this is a matter shared between believers and unbelievers. For the unbeliever affirms the decree and judgment of God, and His eternity and everlastingness. So when he becomes absorbed in this witnessing and is annihilated by it from all else, he has witnessed the reality.

As for his saying "not as acquisition": that is, it is realized at the witnessing of the Reality that witnessing it was not by acquisition, because acquisition is among the actions of the soul. The Reality does not appear while the soul remains, since the Reality is singular, one, and luminous. Therefore the darkness of the soul and seeing its acquisition must disappear, or else he has not witnessed the Reality.

As for abandoning claim, not as knowledge: claim (daʿwa) is attributing a state or other things to your self and your "I-ness." Steadfastness is not valid except by abandoning it, whether it is true or false, for a true claim extinguishes the light of gnosis (maʿrifah). How much more so a false one?

As for his saying "not as knowledge": that is, the thing moving him to abandon claim is not merely his knowledge that claim is corrupt and incompatible with steadfastness. For if he abandons it, his abandonment is because knowledge has forbidden it. Then he is abandoning it outwardly but not in reality, or abandoning it verbally while being engaged in it in state, since he sees that he has fulfilled the right of knowledge in abandoning it. So he abandons it humbly; rather, he abandons it in state and reality, just as one who loves something that harms him abandons his love of it in state and reality. When he realizes that he has no share in the command at all—as God, Mighty and Majestic, said to the best of His creation without exception: ﴿You have no share in the affair﴾ [Al ʿImran: 128]—he abandons claim in witnessing, in reality, and in state.

As for remaining with the light of wakefulness: it is persistence in wakefulness, and that he does not extinguish its light with the darkness of heedlessness, but rather perpetuates his wakefulness. He sees himself in that as one drawn away and taken from himself, guarded by God for him, not that this was attained by his own self-guarding and caution.

These are three matters: wakefulness, its continuation, and witnessing that this is by the Truth, glorified is He, not by you. The cause of his remaining in the light of wakefulness is not his guarding, but God's guarding of him.

It seems the Shaykh is pointing out that steadfastness in this degree is not attained by acquisition, but is purely a gift from God. For he said in the first degree "steadfastness in striving," and in the second "steadfastness of states, not by acquisition nor self-guarding."

His disputing of this is directed: this is something that can be attained by acquisition, by taking the causes that bring their possessor to this station.

Yes, what is negated at this station is the witnessing of acquisition, and that this was attained through his acquisition. So negating acquisition is one thing, and negating the witnessing of it is another.

Perhaps we will elaborate on this matter later, God willing, Exalted is He.

[Section: The Third Degree: Steadfastness by Abandoning the Sight of Steadfastness]

He said: The third degree: steadfastness by abandoning the sight of steadfastness, and by absence from seeking steadfastness through witnessing the Truth's establishing and straightening of the servant.

The meaning of this steadfastness is being oblivious to what is witnessed, from the witnessing of it. So through the witnessed One, the Intended, glorified is He, he is absent from seeing his steadfastness in seeking Him. For seeing steadfastness veils him from the reality of witnessing.

As for absence from seeking steadfastness: it is his absence from seeking it through witnessing that the Truth establishes the servant and straightens him. For when he witnesses that God is the One who establishes him and straightens him, and that his steadfastness and standing are by God, not by himself nor by his seeking, he is absent by this witnessing from feeling his seeking of it.

This measure is among the requirements of witnessing a name whose name is al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting), who subsists by Himself and needs no one, and by whom everything subsists. Everything other than Him is in need of Him in essence. And its need for Him is not caused by origination (huduth), as the theologians (mutakallimun) say, nor by possibility (imkan), as the Peripatetic philosophers (mashsha'un) say. Rather its need for Him is essential, and what is by essence is not caused.

Yes, origination and possibility are indications of need. So explaining by them belongs to the category of definition, not to the category of effective causes. And God knows best.

This descent occurs at death, in the grave, and at resurrection, and the first of the good tidings of the Hereafter comes at death.

(Section)

One of the early Muslims (salaf) said: When the son of Adam rises in the morning, an angel and a devil approach him. If he remembers Allah, glorifies Him, praises Him, and declares His oneness (tahlil), the devil is driven away and the angel takes charge of him. If he begins the day with anything else, the angel leaves him and the devil takes charge of him.

The angel continues to draw near the servant until authority, obedience, and dominance belong to him. The angels then take charge of him during his life, at his death, and at his resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."﴾ [Fussilat: 30-31].

When the angel takes charge of a person, he takes charge of the most sincere, most beneficial, and most righteous of creatures. He makes him firm, teaches him, strengthens his heart, and Allah supports him, as Allah said: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels, "I am with you, so make firm those who have believed"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

So at death the angel says: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of that which will delight you." He makes him firm with the firm word, at the time when he most needs it in this world, at death, and in the grave when he is questioned.

No one is more beneficial to the servant than the companionship of the angel. He is his guardian in his wakefulness and his sleep, in his life, at his death, and in his grave. He is his companion in his loneliness, his friend in his solitude, his interlocutor in his secret thoughts. He fights his enemy on his behalf, defends him, helps him against them, promises him good, gives him good news of it, and urges him to affirm the truth. This is as in the report related both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and as a mawquf (traced to a Companion): "The angel has an inspiration (lamma) in the heart of the son of Adam, and the devil has an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel is a promise of good and affirmation of the promise, and the inspiration of the devil is a promise of evil and denial of the truth."

When the angel draws very near to the servant, he speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the upright word. When the angel withdraws and the devil draws near, the devil speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the word of falsehood and obscenity, until a man is seen speaking with the tongue of an angel, and another speaking with the tongue of a devil.

It is related in a hadith: "Indeed, tranquility (sakinah) speaks upon the tongue of 'Umar" (may Allah be pleased with him). Some of them would hear a good word from a righteous man and say: "Only an angel has cast that upon your tongue." And if they heard its opposite, they would say: "Only a devil has cast that upon your tongue." The angel casts truth into the heart and upon the tongue, while the devil casts falsehood into the heart and sends it onto the tongue.

Among the consequences of sins is that they drive away from the servant his guardian, whose happiness lies in his nearness, neighborhood, and friendship, and they bring near to him his enemy, whose wretchedness, destruction, and corruption lie in his nearness and friendship. To the point that the angel defends the servant and repels on his behalf when a fool insults him and reviles him. Just as two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ), one of them reviling the other while he remained silent. Then he spoke one word in reply to his companion. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I replied to him with some of his own words, you stood up." He said: "The angel was defending you, but when you replied to him, the devil came, and I would not sit with him."

When a Muslim servant prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says "Amin" to his prayer and says: "And for you the same."

When he finishes reciting al-Fatihah, the angels say "Amin" to his supplication.

When a servant who is a monotheist and follows the path and sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) sins, the bearers of the Throne and those around it ask forgiveness for him.

When the servant sleeps in a state of wudu', he spends the night in the protection of an angel.

So the angel of the believer repels evil from him, fights and defends him, teaches him, makes him firm, and encourages him. It is not fitting for a person to mistreat his guardian, to go to great lengths to harm him, to drive him away, or to banish him, for he is his guest and his neighbor.

If honoring the guest is among human obligations, and kindness to the neighbor is among the requirements and demands of faith, then what is the expectation of honoring the most noble of guests and the best and most righteous of neighbors? When a servant harms the angel through various kinds of disobedience, injustice, and immorality, the angel calls down upon him from his Lord and says: "May Allah not reward you with good," just as he prays for him when he honors him with obedience and goodness.

One of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Indeed, there is with you one who never leaves you, so be modest before them and honor them."

No one is more base than the one who is not modest before the Noble, the Mighty in station, nor reveres Him nor honors Him. Allah the Glorified has drawn attention to this meaning with His saying: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12]. That is, be modest before these noble guardians, honor them, and respect them by not letting them see from you what you would be ashamed for another like yourself to see you doing. The angels are hurt by what the children of Adam are hurt by. If the son of Adam is hurt by one who commits immorality and disobedience before him, even if that person does the same deed, then what is the expectation regarding the harm to the noble recording angels? And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

The motivation of religion, compared with the motivation of desire, has three states:

The first: that the dominance and power belong to the call of religion, so the army of desire is turned back in chains. This is attained only through constant patience. Those who reach this rank are the ones granted victory in this world and the Hereafter, and they are those who said: ﴿Our Lord is Allah, then they remained steadfast﴾.

They are those to whom the angels will say at death: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

They are those who attained the companionship of Allah, who is with the patient, and they are those who strove for Allah with the striving due to Him, and whom He singled out for His guidance over all others.

The second state: that the power and dominance belong to the call of desire, so the motivation of religion is completely eliminated, and the wretched one submits to Satan and his troops, who lead him wherever they wish. He has two conditions with them. One is that he becomes one of their soldiers and helpers; this is the state of the weak and powerless. The second is that Satan becomes one of his soldiers; this is the state of the corrupt, dominant sinner and the innovator who is a caller and is followed, as the poet said:

"I was a man of the army of Iblis, then my state rose until Iblis became one of my soldiers."

So Iblis and his troops become his helpers and followers. These are the ones whose wretchedness overcame them, who sold the life of this world for the Hereafter. They reached this state only because they were bankrupt of patience. This state is the state of severe trial, the depth of misery, bad destiny, and the gloating of enemies. Its soldiers are deceit, trickery, false wishes, delusion, procrastination in deeds, long hope, and preferring the immediate over the lasting. About the one who is in this state the Prophet said: "The incapable one is the one who follows his desires and wishes from Allah." The people of this state are of many kinds:

Among them is the one who wars against Allah and His Messenger, striving to extinguish what the Messenger brought, who blocks the way of Allah and seeks to make it crooked and distorted with all his effort, so as to turn people away from it.

Among them is the one who turns away from what the Messenger brought, who is occupied only with his worldly life and its desires.

Among them is the hypocrite with two faces, who earns his living through both disbelief and Islam.

Among them is the frivolous mocker who wastes his breath on lewdness, amusement, and play.

Among them is one who, when admonished, says: "Oh, how I long to repent, but it has become impossible for me, and I have no hope in it."

Among them is one who says: "Allah does not need my prayer or fasting, and I will not be saved by my deeds, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Among them is one who says: "Abandoning sins is a belittling of Allah's pardon and forgiveness."

"So commit as many sins as you can, if you are going to meet the Generous One."

Among them is one who says: "What is my obedience worth compared to what I have done? What benefit is a finger's rescue to a drowning man whose body remains drowned?"

Among them is one who says: "I will repent later, and when death comes and descends upon my courtyard, I will repent, and my repentance will be accepted..."

And other kinds of the deluded whose minds have fallen into the hands of their desires. None of them uses his mind except in the subtle tricks by which he reaches the fulfillment of his lust.

His mind, in the hands of Satan, is like a captive in the hand of an unbeliever, who uses it to tend pigs, press wine, and carry the cross. By subduing his mind and surrendering it to his enemies, he is, in the sight of Allah, like a man who overpowers a Muslim, sells him to the unbelievers, hands him over to them, and makes him their captive.

(Section)

Here is a wondrous point that must be grasped, and the heart should be cleared to reflect upon it. It is that this deluded person, when he humiliated the authority of Allah, by which Allah honored him, raised his rank, and placed him in the hand of the most hateful of His enemies, making him a captive under their domination, control, and authority, Allah then set over him the one whose right it was to have power over him. He placed him under the domination, control, and authority of that enemy, who subjugates him as he wishes, mocks him, and mocks his soldiers and party. Just as he humiliated the authority of Allah and handed it to His enemy, Allah humiliated him and set over him his enemy, whom He had commanded to have power over him, to humiliate and subdue him. He became like one who surrendered himself to his most hostile enemy, who inflicts on him the worst torment. He was about to be taken captive, subdued, and have his rage quenched by his enemy. When he abandoned resistance and fighting and submitted to him, Allah imposed on him that enemy as a punishment. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who make him their ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾

(Section: The Station of Steadfastness)

Section: The Station of Steadfastness

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is the station of steadfastness (istiqamah).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13].

And He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and those who have turned back with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [Hud: 112].

So He clarified that steadfastness is the opposite of transgression, which is exceeding the limits in everything.

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "I am only a human like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God, so take a straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness."﴾ [Fussilat: 6].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had remained upon the way, We would have given them abundant water to test them therein.﴾ [al-Jinn: 16].

The most truthful of this community and the greatest in steadfastness, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), was asked about steadfastness. He said: "That you do not associate anything with Allah." He meant steadfastness upon pure monotheism.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Steadfastness is that you remain steadfast upon the command and the prohibition, and do not swerve like a fox."

'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Istaqamu: they made their deeds sincerely for Allah."

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Istaqamu: they performed the obligatory duties."

Al-Hasan said: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, so they acted in obedience to Him and avoided His disobedience."

Mujahid said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Allah."

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah sanctify his spirit) say: "They remained steadfast upon His love and worship, so they did not turn away from Him to the right or to the left."

In Sahih Muslim, from Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying in Islam about which I will not ask anyone other than you.' He said: 'Say: I believe in Allah, then remain steadfast.'"

Also in it, from Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count it all. And know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none maintains wudu' except a believer."

What is required of the servant is steadfastness, which is rectitude. If he cannot achieve it, then closeness to it (muqarabah). If he falls short of that, then negligence and waste. As in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Be upright and seek closeness to uprightness. And know that none of you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

In this hadith he gathered all the stations of religion. He commanded steadfastness, which is rectitude and correctness in intentions, words, and deeds.

In the hadith of Thawban, he informed that they cannot sustain it, so he moved them to muqarabah, which is that they come close to steadfastness according to their capacity, like one who shoots at a target: if he does not hit it, he comes close to it. Yet with this, he informed them that neither steadfastness nor closeness saves on the Day of Resurrection, so no one should rely on his deed, nor be pleased with it, nor think that his salvation lies in it. Rather, his salvation is only through the mercy, pardon, and grace of Allah.

So steadfastness is a comprehensive word, grasping the totality of religion. It is standing before Allah with the reality of truthfulness and fulfillment of the covenant.

Steadfastness relates to words, actions, states, and intentions. In steadfastness regarding them is that they are for Allah, through Allah, and upon the command of Allah.

Some of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: "Be a possessor of steadfastness (istiqamah), not a seeker of miracles (karamah). For your soul is restless in seeking miracles, while your Lord demands of you steadfastness."

And I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God sanctify his spirit, say: "The greatest of miracles is adherence to steadfastness."

[Section: The Degrees of Steadfastness]

[The First Degree: Steadfastness in striving with moderation (iqtisad)]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree: steadfastness in striving with moderation (iqtisad). Neither being content with the mere outward form of knowledge (rasm al-ʿilm), nor exceeding the bounds of sincerity (ikhlas), nor opposing the way of the Sunnah (nahj al-Sunnah).

This degree comprises six matters: action (ʿamal) and striving (ijtihad) in it, which is the exertion of effort; and moderation (iqtisad), which is walking between the two extremes of excess (ifrat), namely oppressing the souls, and deficiency (tafrit) through neglect; and halting at what knowledge has drawn (yarsumuhu al-ʿilm), not halting at the call of the moment (daʿi al-hal); and singling out the One Worshipped with intention, which is sincerity; and the actions conforming to the command, which is following the Sunnah.

By these six matters the steadfastness of the people of this degree is completed. By departing from any one of them they depart from steadfastness: either a total departure or a partial departure.

The predecessors (salaf) often mention these two principles, namely moderation in actions and holding fast to the Sunnah, for Satan smells the heart of the servant and tests it. If he sees in it a call to innovation (bidʿah) and an aversion from full submission to the Sunnah, he removes it from holding fast to it. If he sees in it eagerness for the Sunnah and intense pursuit of it, he does not succeed through cutting it off from the Sunnah, so he orders it to strive, to oppress the soul, and to exceed the limit of moderation in it, saying: "This is good and obedience, and increase and striving in it is more perfect." So do not slacken with those who slacken, nor sleep with those who sleep. He does not cease urging and inciting him until he takes him out of moderation in it, so he exits its limit, just as the first one exits this limit. Likewise this other one exits the other limit.

This is the condition of the Khawarij, whom the people of steadfastness regard as belittling their prayer alongside their prayer, their fasting alongside their fasting, and their recitation alongside their recitation. Both matters are a departure from the Sunnah into innovation. But this one leads to the innovation of deficiency and neglect, and the other to the innovation of excess and extravagance.

And one of the predecessors said: "God has not commanded any command except that Satan has in it two tendencies: either toward deficiency (tafrit), or toward exceeding the bounds, which is excess (ifrat); and he does not care which of the two he attains: increase or decrease."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may God be pleased with them both: "O ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, every doer has a surge of zeal (shirrah), and every surge has a lull (fatrah). Whoever's lull is toward the Sunnah has succeeded, and whoever's lull is toward innovation has perished and lost." He said this to him when he ordered him to moderation in action.

So all good lies in striving with moderation, and sincerity joined with following. As one of the Companions said: "Moderation on the path and the Sunnah is better than striving in opposition to the path and the Sunnah. So be eager that your actions be upon the methodology of the Prophets, peace be upon them, and their Sunnah."

Likewise, showing off (riyaʾ) in actions removes one from steadfastness, and so does lassitude and laxity (futur wa tawani).

[Section: The Second Degree: Steadfastness of States (istiqamat al-ahwal)]

He said: The second degree is steadfastness of states (ahwal). It is witnessing the Reality (shuhud al-haqiqah) not as acquisition (kasb); abandoning claim (rafd al-daʿwa) not as knowledge (ʿilm); and remaining with the light of wakefulness (yaqazah) not as self-guarding (tahaffuz).

He means that the steadfastness of the state is by these three.

As for witnessing the Reality: the Reality is of two realities: a cosmic reality (haqiqah kawniyyah) and a religious reality (haqiqah diniyyah), and a third reality gathers them, which is their source, their origin, and their end. Most of the practitioners of the path (arbab al-suluk) among the later ones only mean by the Reality the cosmic reality. Witnessing it is witnessing the singularity of the Lord in action, and that all else is a locus for the flow of His rulings and His acts. It is like a ditch which is merely a place for water to flow through.

They believe that witnessing this reality and annihilation (fana') in it is the ultimate goal of the wayfarers.

Among them are those who witness the reality of eternity (azaliyyah) and perpetuity, and the annihilation and folding of contingent things within the expanse of eternity and everlastingness, and their dissolving therein. So they witness them as non-existent, and witness the singularity of their Originator with true existence through the Truth, and that the existence of all else is traces and shadows.

The first witnessed His singularity in acts; this one witnessed His singularity in existence.

The possessor of the religious reality is in another stage, for he is in the station of command and prohibition, reward and punishment, loyalty and enmity, and the distinction between what God loves and is pleased with, and what He hates and is angered by. He is in the station of the second distinction (al-farq al-thani), which the servant does not attain the level of Islam—let alone the station of ihsan—except by it.

Whoever turns away from it entirely has no share in Islam whatsoever. He is like the one whom al-Junayd used to advise his companions about, saying: "Hold fast to the second distinction." It was called "second" because the first distinction is a distinction by nature and the self, while this is a distinction by the command.

Unification (jamʿ) is also of two kinds: unification within distinction (jamʿ fi farq), which is the unification of the people of steadfastness and monotheism; and unification without distinction (jamʿ bila farq), which is the unification of the people of heresy (zandaqah) and atheism (ilhad).

So people are of three types: the possessor of distinction without unification, who is blameworthy, deficient, and forsaken.

The possessor of unification without distinction, which is the unification of the people of heresy and atheism: his companion is an atheist heretic (zindiq).

The possessor of distinction and unification: he witnesses the distinction within the unification and the multiplicity within the oneness. He is the upright monotheist who distinguishes. This is the possessor of the third reality, which gathers the religious and the cosmic realities. Witnessing this gathering reality is the very essence of steadfastness.

As for witnessing the cosmic reality, or the eternal one, and annihilation in it: this is a matter shared between believers and unbelievers. For the unbeliever affirms the decree and judgment of God, and His eternity and everlastingness. So when he becomes absorbed in this witnessing and is annihilated by it from all else, he has witnessed the reality.

As for his saying "not as acquisition": that is, it is realized at the witnessing of the Reality that witnessing it was not by acquisition, because acquisition is among the actions of the soul. The Reality does not appear while the soul remains, since the Reality is singular, one, and luminous. Therefore the darkness of the soul and seeing its acquisition must disappear, or else he has not witnessed the Reality.

As for abandoning claim, not as knowledge: claim (daʿwa) is attributing a state or other things to your self and your "I-ness." Steadfastness is not valid except by abandoning it, whether it is true or false, for a true claim extinguishes the light of gnosis (maʿrifah). How much more so a false one?

As for his saying "not as knowledge": that is, the thing moving him to abandon claim is not merely his knowledge that claim is corrupt and incompatible with steadfastness. For if he abandons it, his abandonment is because knowledge has forbidden it. Then he is abandoning it outwardly but not in reality, or abandoning it verbally while being engaged in it in state, since he sees that he has fulfilled the right of knowledge in abandoning it. So he abandons it humbly; rather, he abandons it in state and reality, just as one who loves something that harms him abandons his love of it in state and reality. When he realizes that he has no share in the command at all—as God, Mighty and Majestic, said to the best of His creation without exception: ﴿You have no share in the affair﴾ [Al ʿImran: 128]—he abandons claim in witnessing, in reality, and in state.

As for remaining with the light of wakefulness: it is persistence in wakefulness, and that he does not extinguish its light with the darkness of heedlessness, but rather perpetuates his wakefulness. He sees himself in that as one drawn away and taken from himself, guarded by God for him, not that this was attained by his own self-guarding and caution.

These are three matters: wakefulness, its continuation, and witnessing that this is by the Truth, glorified is He, not by you. The cause of his remaining in the light of wakefulness is not his guarding, but God's guarding of him.

It seems the Shaykh is pointing out that steadfastness in this degree is not attained by acquisition, but is purely a gift from God. For he said in the first degree "steadfastness in striving," and in the second "steadfastness of states, not by acquisition nor self-guarding."

His disputing of this is directed: this is something that can be attained by acquisition, by taking the causes that bring their possessor to this station.

Yes, what is negated at this station is the witnessing of acquisition, and that this was attained through his acquisition. So negating acquisition is one thing, and negating the witnessing of it is another.

Perhaps we will elaborate on this matter later, God willing, Exalted is He.

[Section: The Third Degree: Steadfastness by Abandoning the Sight of Steadfastness]

He said: The third degree: steadfastness by abandoning the sight of steadfastness, and by absence from seeking steadfastness through witnessing the Truth's establishing and straightening of the servant.

The meaning of this steadfastness is being oblivious to what is witnessed, from the witnessing of it. So through the witnessed One, the Intended, glorified is He, he is absent from seeing his steadfastness in seeking Him. For seeing steadfastness veils him from the reality of witnessing.

As for absence from seeking steadfastness: it is his absence from seeking it through witnessing that the Truth establishes the servant and straightens him. For when he witnesses that God is the One who establishes him and straightens him, and that his steadfastness and standing are by God, not by himself nor by his seeking, he is absent by this witnessing from feeling his seeking of it.

This measure is among the requirements of witnessing a name whose name is al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting), who subsists by Himself and needs no one, and by whom everything subsists. Everything other than Him is in need of Him in essence. And its need for Him is not caused by origination (huduth), as the theologians (mutakallimun) say, nor by possibility (imkan), as the Peripatetic philosophers (mashsha'un) say. Rather its need for Him is essential, and what is by essence is not caused.

Yes, origination and possibility are indications of need. So explaining by them belongs to the category of definition, not to the category of effective causes. And God knows best.

This descent occurs at death, in the grave, and at resurrection, and the first of the good tidings of the Hereafter comes at death.

(Section)

One of the early Muslims (salaf) said: When the son of Adam rises in the morning, an angel and a devil approach him. If he remembers Allah, glorifies Him, praises Him, and declares His oneness (tahlil), the devil is driven away and the angel takes charge of him. If he begins the day with anything else, the angel leaves him and the devil takes charge of him.

The angel continues to draw near the servant until authority, obedience, and dominance belong to him. The angels then take charge of him during his life, at his death, and at his resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."﴾ [Fussilat: 30-31].

When the angel takes charge of a person, he takes charge of the most sincere, most beneficial, and most righteous of creatures. He makes him firm, teaches him, strengthens his heart, and Allah supports him, as Allah said: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels, "I am with you, so make firm those who have believed"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

So at death the angel says: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of that which will delight you." He makes him firm with the firm word, at the time when he most needs it in this world, at death, and in the grave when he is questioned.

No one is more beneficial to the servant than the companionship of the angel. He is his guardian in his wakefulness and his sleep, in his life, at his death, and in his grave. He is his companion in his loneliness, his friend in his solitude, his interlocutor in his secret thoughts. He fights his enemy on his behalf, defends him, helps him against them, promises him good, gives him good news of it, and urges him to affirm the truth. This is as in the report related both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and as a mawquf (traced to a Companion): "The angel has an inspiration (lamma) in the heart of the son of Adam, and the devil has an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel is a promise of good and affirmation of the promise, and the inspiration of the devil is a promise of evil and denial of the truth."

When the angel draws very near to the servant, he speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the upright word. When the angel withdraws and the devil draws near, the devil speaks upon his tongue and places upon it the word of falsehood and obscenity, until a man is seen speaking with the tongue of an angel, and another speaking with the tongue of a devil.

It is related in a hadith: "Indeed, tranquility (sakinah) speaks upon the tongue of 'Umar" (may Allah be pleased with him). Some of them would hear a good word from a righteous man and say: "Only an angel has cast that upon your tongue." And if they heard its opposite, they would say: "Only a devil has cast that upon your tongue." The angel casts truth into the heart and upon the tongue, while the devil casts falsehood into the heart and sends it onto the tongue.

Among the consequences of sins is that they drive away from the servant his guardian, whose happiness lies in his nearness, neighborhood, and friendship, and they bring near to him his enemy, whose wretchedness, destruction, and corruption lie in his nearness and friendship. To the point that the angel defends the servant and repels on his behalf when a fool insults him and reviles him. Just as two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ), one of them reviling the other while he remained silent. Then he spoke one word in reply to his companion. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I replied to him with some of his own words, you stood up." He said: "The angel was defending you, but when you replied to him, the devil came, and I would not sit with him."

When a Muslim servant prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says "Amin" to his prayer and says: "And for you the same."

When he finishes reciting al-Fatihah, the angels say "Amin" to his supplication.

When a servant who is a monotheist and follows the path and sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) sins, the bearers of the Throne and those around it ask forgiveness for him.

When the servant sleeps in a state of wudu', he spends the night in the protection of an angel.

So the angel of the believer repels evil from him, fights and defends him, teaches him, makes him firm, and encourages him. It is not fitting for a person to mistreat his guardian, to go to great lengths to harm him, to drive him away, or to banish him, for he is his guest and his neighbor.

If honoring the guest is among human obligations, and kindness to the neighbor is among the requirements and demands of faith, then what is the expectation of honoring the most noble of guests and the best and most righteous of neighbors? When a servant harms the angel through various kinds of disobedience, injustice, and immorality, the angel calls down upon him from his Lord and says: "May Allah not reward you with good," just as he prays for him when he honors him with obedience and goodness.

One of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Indeed, there is with you one who never leaves you, so be modest before them and honor them."

No one is more base than the one who is not modest before the Noble, the Mighty in station, nor reveres Him nor honors Him. Allah the Glorified has drawn attention to this meaning with His saying: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12]. That is, be modest before these noble guardians, honor them, and respect them by not letting them see from you what you would be ashamed for another like yourself to see you doing. The angels are hurt by what the children of Adam are hurt by. If the son of Adam is hurt by one who commits immorality and disobedience before him, even if that person does the same deed, then what is the expectation regarding the harm to the noble recording angels? And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

The motivation of religion, compared with the motivation of desire, has three states:

The first: that the dominance and power belong to the call of religion, so the army of desire is turned back in chains. This is attained only through constant patience. Those who reach this rank are the ones granted victory in this world and the Hereafter, and they are those who said: ﴿Our Lord is Allah, then they remained steadfast﴾.

They are those to whom the angels will say at death: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

They are those who attained the companionship of Allah, who is with the patient, and they are those who strove for Allah with the striving due to Him, and whom He singled out for His guidance over all others.

The second state: that the power and dominance belong to the call of desire, so the motivation of religion is completely eliminated, and the wretched one submits to Satan and his troops, who lead him wherever they wish. He has two conditions with them. One is that he becomes one of their soldiers and helpers; this is the state of the weak and powerless. The second is that Satan becomes one of his soldiers; this is the state of the corrupt, dominant sinner and the innovator who is a caller and is followed, as the poet said:

"I was a man of the army of Iblis, then my state rose until Iblis became one of my soldiers."

So Iblis and his troops become his helpers and followers. These are the ones whose wretchedness overcame them, who sold the life of this world for the Hereafter. They reached this state only because they were bankrupt of patience. This state is the state of severe trial, the depth of misery, bad destiny, and the gloating of enemies. Its soldiers are deceit, trickery, false wishes, delusion, procrastination in deeds, long hope, and preferring the immediate over the lasting. About the one who is in this state the Prophet said: "The incapable one is the one who follows his desires and wishes from Allah." The people of this state are of many kinds:

Among them is the one who wars against Allah and His Messenger, striving to extinguish what the Messenger brought, who blocks the way of Allah and seeks to make it crooked and distorted with all his effort, so as to turn people away from it.

Among them is the one who turns away from what the Messenger brought, who is occupied only with his worldly life and its desires.

Among them is the hypocrite with two faces, who earns his living through both disbelief and Islam.
